answer:
1. The animation shows a historical case where buying a home in June 2006 left the buyer worse off than renting. It calls this "the darkest house." It's built from FHFA home prices, BLS rents and Freddie Mac mortgage rates, and it's labeled "ILLUSTRATIVE."

2. Only the text changes across the six frames. In frames 1 and 2, the title "The darkest house" sits above a dark house labeled "June 2006." From frame 3 on, the title is replaced by "$82,385 behind," and "All $ in dollars of the day" appears in the footer. The row of houses along the bottom stays the same. The legend says lit houses mean the buyer is ahead after ten years, and dark houses mean the renter is ahead. Most houses on the left are dark. Most on the right are lit.

3. It means that someone who bought in June 2006 was about $82,385 behind a renter after ten years. That figure is in nominal dollars. The bad result came from the timing of the purchase. The footer says this is US-only and "history, not a forecast." The lit houses on the right suggest that buying at other times came out ahead.

4. The animation gives no direct advice. A viewer might take away that the answer to rent versus buy depends on when you buy, and that buying doesn't always win. You shouldn't read it as a prediction, because the footer rules that out.

5. The picture and on-screen text did not give any advice. The takeaway in point 4 is my own reading. The animation only shows the data and the "history, not a forecast" caveat.
